whyTitle.message: Why is the UI not embedded in the side panel?

whyBody.message: The dsh web session cookie is HttpOnly; SameSite=Strict. Inside an extension side panel it belongs to a cross-site iframe: the token exchange and ordinary requests do carry the cookie, but the WebSocket handshake does not — and every DSH RPC travels over WebSocket (the handshake is refused with 401 and the socket closes with 1006). The same page opened as a top-level window carries the cookie normally, so the UI runs in a window.

whyFootnote.message: This extension proxies nothing and never rewrites DSH cookies or signatures; it only opens and focuses.

optionsLead.message: Configure which dsh web server the Edge side panel connects to, and manage the window that hosts the UI.

autoOpenLabel.message: Open the DSH window automatically when the browser starts

notesBody.message: The DSH session cookie is HttpOnly; SameSite=Strict, and each process prints a one-time ?token=… . A top-level window is the only place this extension can guarantee a working WebSocket session: in a cross-site iframe inside the side panel, ordinary requests carry the cookie but the WebSocket handshake does not, so every DSH RPC fails.

notesFootnote.message: The extension does not proxy, does not rewrite cookies, and does not modify DSH; it only opens and focuses the window. The token is cleared from storage right after it is exchanged.
